correctness.rationale: The finite K4 obstruction enumeration exhausts all vertex splits (4 new, 3 new plus 1 old, 2 new plus 2 old, 1 new plus 3 old), including each \(H[U]\) and \(H[V]\) triangle obstruction. A shared hub fixes C once and all petals factor, yielding the exact finite sum. At C empty the pair-of-subsets state model gives the weighted independent-set upper bound, with equality for triangle-free H. The complementary graph has \(\binom r2-k\) edges; the colex form of Kruskal-Katona maximizes every clique coefficient, and its complement is exactly a k-star for \(1\le k\le r-1\). Positive weights and an (r-1)-element independent set force the sole maximizing shape. There is a strict gap for any additional edge, for nonstar graphs, and between C nonempty and empty. This justifies the sharp exponential equivalence with the exact combinatorial multiplicity. Direct forbidden-K4 enumerations checked 88 finite cases and 432 weighted extremal comparisons; tests support but do not prove unbounded claims.

value.rationale: The natural induced friendship base has a single globally shared hub, causing type counts to couple across petals. Exact transfer separates that global state from independent petal choices, while a nontrivial Kruskal-Katona extremal argument classifies all rare internal-edge layers, not just two edges: at every \(k\le r-1\), fixed k, the conditional type graph becomes a k-star with an exact exponential rarity and multiplicity. This is a structural explanation of clustering in the higher-arity orbit spectrum, with a direct contrast to prior disjoint-clique bases; unary and pair facts alone are not presented as new, and the theorem is not a routine substitution of parameters.
